images.seen: Africa broadly right; the Lado Enclave is drawn as Anglo-Egyptian Sudan although the Free State held it, Darfur is only the 981-cell Cliopatria core with 771 cells of the Darfur states drawn as the Sudan's (then nobody's from 1903), and a leftover of the Egyptian Khedivate sits in north Darfur.

Horn: Dervish State, Majeerteen, Hobyo and Italian Somalia plausible; about 78 cells of the Harar and Jijiga highlands still drawn as the Khedivate of Egypt (cleared once the p1890-p1899 ruling is compiled).

Europe and the Near East right (Sweden and Norway separate, Crete Greek, Bosnia Austro-Hungarian, Bulgaria drawn independent); Bulgaria is still tinted an Ottoman vassal at the end of 1908 by the hierarchy row.
East and South-East Asia right except unowned land: Aceh at the head of Sumatra, most of Sulawesi until 1908, and a 22-cell hole at Tianjin in the Qing's own coast.

Darfur now whole as the Sultanate of Darfur, the Lado Enclave now the Congo Free State's; a large unowned block in western Ethiopia (Wollega, Illubabor, Beni Shangul) remains until 1908, see problems.
Aceh now Dutch East Indies; Sumatra whole.

issues.what: Lado Enclave drawn as Anglo-Egyptian Sudan 1900-1909 (the Sudan, 13 cells smaller than the Free State, won the size rule at its founding of 1899 and again against the Belgian Congo in 1908: 366 cell-years). The page has the Free State in occupation through the window and the Sudan taking the enclave only on 10 June 1910.

Darfur: 771 cells of the five Darfur states left to the Anglo-Egyptian Sudan in 1900-1902 and to nobody from 1903 (the Sudan's keyframes are 'without Darfur'; 842-cell snap of 1903), plus 76 cells of north Darfur still the Khedivate of Egypt's. The page has Ali Dinar's rule recognised and tolerated until the British conquest of 1916.

Aceh (129 cells) and nothing else drawn as nobody's from 1905 to 1909: the ledger gives it to the Dutch East Indies in 1904 but the Cliopatria shapes of 1905 and 1908 omit it (the 1914 shape has it), so the snaps empty it.

Hole of 22 cells (15 from 1905) around Tianjin: Cliopatria's Qing shapes of 1900-1904 and 1905-1910 leave the city out and no dossier fills it, so it is unowned for the whole window. The page has the city under a foreign provisional government 1900-1902, handed back to the Qing on 15 August 1902.

Ethiopian-empire / khedivate-of-egypt (237 cell-years, Egypt winning): 78 cells of the Harar and Jijiga highlands drawn as Egyptian although Egyptian rule at Harar ended in 1884 and Shewa annexed it after Chelenqo (1887). The p1890-p1899 patch (rulings/0, Ethiopia over Egypt 1890-1899) already clears them from the 1 January 1900 anchor in my trial, so my own loss event was redundant and was withdrawn before writing.

Emirate of Jabal Shammar over the Ottoman Empire (308 cell-years: Al Jawf, Tayma and Khaybar, Tabuk edge). The Rashidi dossier (ledger/5) itself holds al-Jawf, Tayma and Khaybar from Muhammad's expansion, with a page.

Qassim goes to the Third Saudi State in 1905 (200-cell snap of emirate-of-nejd_1905) but the Rashidi ledger dates its loss to 13 April 1906: a one-year disagreement between a Cliopatria shape and the ledger.

problems: hierarchy: principality-of-bulgaria,ottoman-empire,1878,1908,vassal: Bulgaria declared independence on 5 October 1908 (page https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Principality_of_Bulgaria, 'Independence: 5 October 1908'; the dossier's own vassal_end is 1908-10) but the row ends after 1908, so the end-of-1908 map still tints Bulgaria as an Ottoman vassal (376 cells close at 1909). If year-end maps are the rule, 'to' should be 1907.

ethiopian-empire_1900 (and probably ethiopian-empire_1905): suggested keyframe override, copy the p1890-p1899 keyframe_overrides/4 (ethiopian-empire_1898) correction with {"cliopatria": "Ethiopian Empire", "year": 1900} (and 1905) in place of 1898, source https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Menelik_II, so the Cliopatria shape no longer removes the pre-1900 conquests (398 cells removed in the 1900 snap). Not done by me: all 8 pages were spent.

qing-dynasty_1911 (window p1910-p1919): the Cliopatria shape of 1911 has the same Tianjin hole (10 cells of the 37 within 45 km), so its 1911 snap will empty Tianjin again; apply the same union {"place": "Tianjin", "km": 45} there.

belgian-congo/ledger/1 (1910, window p1910-p1919): the loss of Central Equatoria names british-africa as counterpart, not anglo-egyptian-sudan, so the Lado cells go to British Africa before the Sudan's own 1910 gain finds nothing to take; a patch event or ruling in p1910-p1919 should name the Sudan.

Crossing into the next window: keyframe_overrides/3 replaces dutch-east-indies_1908, a keyframe that runs 1908-1913; it only acts at its start year (1908) but the p1910-p1919 agent should know Aceh is in it. The Cliopatria Dutch East Indies shape of 1914 already holds Aceh.

In my trial (other windows' patch files included) the united-states-of-america_1900 snap removes 770 cells (Michigan 405, Wisconsin 109, Alaska 70: Great Lakes cells held in the 1 January 1900 anchor and dropped by the 1900 shape) and french-africa_1900 removes 759 (was 279); both come from other windows' patches or later dossier edits, not mine, and the lakes end up unowned as in the published draft.

lado enclave extent: the gazetteer region 'Lado Enclave' (119 cells, 30,095 km2) is used for the event and ruling; the dossiers use all of Central Equatoria (183 cells), the page gives about 39,000 km2. 85 Central Equatoria cells east of the Nile stay with the Sudan, and the British Africa 1905 shape takes 11 southern cells of the enclave from the Free State (R1).
